responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the VAX architecture, covering both core VAX code generation and the operating-system/ABI variants built on top of it. Its central machine description and support code define how GCC represents VAX condition codes and floating-point modes, matches operands and addressing forms, expands and recognizes RTL patterns, selects instructions, and emits assembly for integer, floating-point, branch, stack, block-move, builtin, and atomic operations. The main target implementation and headers provide the ABI and calling-convention rules, register set, storage layout, frame and prologue logic, trampoline/thunk handling, address legitimacy and cost modeling, and other target hooks that connect generic RTL generation to VAX-specific semantics. Around that core, option files declare VAX tuning and syntax switches, while ELF/Linux/NetBSD/OpenBSD headers adapt the backend to particular object formats and system conventions by adjusting specs, predefined macros, linker/assembler behavior, data-model details, PIC handling, and exception/debug settings. Overall, this module is responsible for translating GCC’s generic RTL into correct VAX machine code and system-specific binaries.
